public_rationale: Marcus's qualified reporting claim is supported. Contemporaneous coverage explicitly attributed a $100 billion profit-generation criterion to The Information. The coverage described an agreement already made, which is stronger than considering one. The important qualification is scope: it concerned an internal contractual criterion and the ability to generate profits. The same article distinguished OpenAI's public definition, so it does not support a broader claim that cognition had been removed from every OpenAI definition.
limitations: Support is for the attributed reporting claim, not independent verification of the private agreement.
The evidence is secondary reporting because the original pages were inaccessible.
Reading purely in terms of profits as a universal replacement would leave that broader proposition unresolved.

our_interpretation: The qualified wording primarily asserts the existence of reporting about a profit-linked AGI definition involving Microsoft and OpenAI.
The target period is the late-2024 reporting episode referenced in context through publication, not a period in which OpenAI earned profits.
The threshold concerns the capacity to generate profits, not profits already realized.
Support for the reported contractual definition does not establish replacement of every public or scientific AGI definition.
The financial scope records a reported capability threshold. No fiscal period, annualization or gross-versus-net accounting calculation is specified.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous reputable reporting attributes to The Information a Microsoft–OpenAI AGI criterion based on AI systems capable of generating $100 billion in profits.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The cited reporting did not describe such a criterion, concerned a materially different amount or financial measure, or was credibly corrected or disproved.
